reason: Twenty-two thousand is more than a month and a half of what we earn, and every rupee is going to the wedding fund right now. I already have an inverter and battery, so I would rather hand-wash or put a cheap washer on the inverter than pay for a second battery inside a machine.
objection: I am paying again for a battery when I already own one. Two loads per charge is not much, and if the lithium battery dies after three years in our heat I am stuck with a dealer bill I cannot afford.
would_change_my_mind: A version without the built-in battery, made to run well off my existing inverter or solar, for under ₹12,000, or an EMI around ₹800 a month.
